decision.required_when: the source explicitly qualifies the observation by one selected forward gear
decision.empty_means: the source does not qualify the observation by a selected gear

existing_dimensions_reused.speed_interval: The 80-120 km/h interval is part of the canonical attribute meaning.
existing_dimensions_reused.fuel: Fuel-dependent alternatives use the existing configuration_attribute_values.fuel_type_code field.
existing_dimensions_reused.passenger_layout: Five- and seven-seat distinctions target exact configurations and reuse canonical number_of_seats data.
existing_dimensions_reused.powertrain_and_transmission: Powertrain and transmission are properties of the exact target configuration.

source_evidence.notes: The table gives fourth- and fifth-gear 80-120 km/h values, including separate LPG and petrol columns for Eco-G 120.
The table gives fourth-, fifth- and sixth-gear values where stated; the automatic Eco-G column states only fourth-gear values.
The table states fourth-gear elasticity separately for exact five- and seven-seat variants and separates LPG and petrol where the powertrain is bi-fuel.

planned_semantics.automatic_transmissions: A gear number is valid for an automatic transmission only when the source explicitly names that gear.
planned_semantics.gear_count: Do not derive gear_number from gear_count and do not infer missing gears from the transmission specification.
planned_semantics.blank_value: Blank is not unknown, all gears, top gear or not applicable.

planned_validation: gear_number is empty or a canonical positive integer
a populated gear_number is allowed only for an explicitly eligible performance attribute
gear-distinct values may share configuration, attribute, fuel, date and source
two rows with the same complete observation identity and date remain a semantic collision
reporting and latest-value selection include gear_number in their keys
existing_data_policy: Existing elasticity observations without explicit gear context remain unchanged and retain an empty gear_number after schema migration.
No current configuration value, range, availability record, price or source relationship is changed by this modeling package.

rejected_alternatives.reason: Codes such as elasticity_80_120_4th_gear duplicate one fact and make comparison across gears harder.
A separate table is disproportionate for one scalar qualifier already analogous to observation-level fuel context.
The reviewed evidence does not justify an untyped all-purpose context architecture.
Those dimensions already exist on the value row or exact configuration and must not be repeated.

next_package.name: Brochure Gear-Specific Performance Schema Foundation
next_package.goal: Add the optional gear_number column, validation, import-spec, SQLite, data-dictionary and reporting support without importing brochure elasticity values.
